review.title: CI executes every script suite the repository declares, and a failing validate job says something
review.acceptance:
CREATED ON gpt-architect's ROUND-107 DIRECTIVE. Two defects, one file.

A. EVERY SUITE THE REPOSITORY DECLARES IS EXECUTED BY CI. The validate job mirrors `npm run test:scripts` as separate named steps, and its own comment says 'a FIFTH script added to it must be added here too' -- and then records that the drift it warns about had already happened once. It has happened twice more: `test:scripts` now names SIX scripts and this job runs FOUR of them. `scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs` and `node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs` (30 cases) are in the alias and in no step. `apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs` (17 cases) is in no alias and no step and is run by nothing at all.
REQUIRED: all three execute in CI and fail the build when they fail.
REQUIRED: the mirror is kept in step BY A MECHANISM, not by a comment asking a human to remember. A note that a hand-kept list must be kept in step is already in the file, it did not keep the list in step, and a fourth occurrence of the same drift is not a thing to apologise for again.
REQUIRED: the added suites run where their dependencies allow. The six pre-install steps are pre-install on purpose -- they use Node builtins only, so a dependency failure cannot mask a control-plane or structure failure -- and a suite placed there must actually hold to that.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: 'do not turn apps/desktop into a workspace if that causes validators to traverse generated packaging output'. Round 106 measured exactly that and it does: a dependency-free apps/desktop/package.json costs 8 lockfile lines and turbo picks the suite up, but `validate-workspace-deps.mjs` then walks apps/desktop/sidecar/server/ -- generated packaging output carrying its own .gitignore of '*' -- and demands the manifest declare `next`. The measurement is in coordination/WINDOWS_LIFECYCLE_WIRING.md section 8.

B. A FAILING `validate` JOB SAYS SOMETHING ACTIONABLE. On run 37028642916 at 30cef6e the job aborted at 10m 38s with one annotation, 'Process completed with exit code 134', naming no step -- having PASSED at 25m 4s and 27m 29s on the two runs before it. Exit 134 is SIGABRT. The engineering session cannot read run logs or download artifacts (the Actions API answers 403) and so could not determine which step aborted, let alone why; two local reproductions of the prime suspect passed, at 1261s ambient and 1807s under a runner-like heap cap.
REQUIRED: a run page carries enough to tell a reader WHICH step aborted and under what machine conditions -- at minimum core count, total and available memory, free disk, the Node version and NODE_OPTIONS -- without needing the log or the artifact.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: 'DO NOT declare OOM. DO NOT increase memory merely because exit 134 occurred. DO NOT increase timeouts without evidence. DO NOT add retries to hide it. Improve diagnostics first.' Nothing in this task may change what CI runs or how much it is given. Diagnostics only.
REQUIRED, and quoted from the directive: no secret leakage. Nothing added here may print the environment wholesale, a token, or a value this repository has not already published; an allowlist of named variables, never a dump.

C. THE JOB'S COST DOES NOT GROW MATERIALLY. The three added suites take under a second between them locally. Diagnostics must stay cheap enough that nobody is tempted to remove them the next time the job is slow.
review.notes:
CREATED IN ROUND 107 on the commander's relay of gpt-architect's directive, which named the task id, the write surface and the review dependencies. THE ACCEPTANCE TEXT ABOVE IS CLAUDE'S RENDERING of the requirements in that directive, not a transcription of it -- the two passages in quotation marks are verbatim and everything else is Claude's wording of what the directive asked for. Correct it in review if the rendering is wider or narrower than intended.

THE LANE IS A CHOICE AND IT IS DECLARED RATHER THAN BURIED. Two candidate lanes were considered.
  - INFRA is the obvious reading of 'CI workflow' and it is where PW-0501 sat, because PW-0501's subject was producing a Windows build artifact.
  - INTEGRATION is what was chosen. The subject here is not a pipeline capability: it is that components which already exist -- three test suites, all passing, all committed -- are not connected to the build graph, and that a job's failure is not legible to the people who have to act on it. That is wiring, and this repository has never treated .github/workflows/ as Infra-exclusive: PL-AI-0003 added the dispatcher step to this same file under lane Coordination, and PL-0704 and PW-0312 both wrote ci.yml under lane Frontend. Lane has followed subject matter here, not file path.
THE CONFOUND, STATED BECAUSE IT IS REAL: claude-infra is at maxParallel 1 and the slot is held by PW-0208 in REVIEW, so Integration is also the lane with capacity. Round 105 forbade re-laning a task to obtain an idle agent and that prohibition is respected on its own terms -- nothing was moved -- but a new task's lane chosen while one candidate is busy deserves the disclosure rather than the silence. Re-lane it to Infra in review if the reasoning above does not hold; nothing in the implementation depends on the lane.

CONFLICTS, CHECKED IN BOTH FIELDS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE CREATION. .github/workflows/ci.yml: written by PL-0001, PL-0704, PL-AI-0002 and PW-0312, all DONE; read by PL-AI-0003, PW-0102, PW-0501 and PL-0406, all DONE. No open task holds it in either field. package.json is in PW-0503's allowedPaths (READY, unowned) -- holding it here as a READ-ONLY reviewDependency reserves nothing, and the cost is recorded: if PW-0503 is later claimed and writes package.json, it stales any approval of this task computed before that write. scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs is under PW-0502's and PW-0503's allowedPaths (both READY, unowned), again read-only here. apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs is under PW-0208's allowedPaths and PW-0208 IS ACTIVE, in REVIEW -- so this task must not write it, and it does not: it is a reviewDependency. The reverse direction matters more and is clear: this task's only write is ci.yml, which PW-0208 names in neither field, so claiming this cannot stale PW-0208's pending review.

WHY THE ORPHANED-SUITE HALF IS NOT SOLVED BY MAKING apps/desktop A WORKSPACE: measured in round 106 and reverted. See acceptance clause A.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck: 22 tasks successful, 22 total. STATED PLAINLY: no TypeScript project compiles .github/workflows/ci.yml, so this records that nothing else was disturbed and nothing about the change. The evidence that bears on the change is under the unit gate.

unit.evidence:
THE TURBO RESULT FIRST, WITH ITS LIMITATION. 'npm run test': 22 tasks successful, 22 total, 47.4s, FULL TURBO -- every task served from cache, because the change touches no workspace. A fully cached pass is evidence of no collateral damage and of nothing else; recording it without saying so would be the weaker claim dressed as the stronger one.

THE EVIDENCE THAT BEARS ON THE CHANGE WAS PRODUCED BY RUNNING IT.

1. THE THREE PREVIOUSLY-UNRUN SUITES, executed exactly as the new steps invoke them. node scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs: 9 assertions, exit 0. node --test scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs: 30 pass, 0 fail. node --test apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs: 17 pass, 0 fail. All three are Node-builtins-and-git only, which is why they sit with the pre-install group.

2. THE MIRROR CHECK, PROVED BY ITS FAILURES RATHER THAN ITS PASS. Extracted from the YAML by a parser and run four ways.
   - Against the current tree: 'test:scripts names 6 suite(s) ... every suite in the alias has a step in this job', exit 0.
   - AGAINST THE ci.yml AS IT STOOD AT HEAD (git show HEAD:.github/workflows/ci.yml, with the current package.json): exit 1, naming scripts/test-desktop-target.mjs and scripts/windows/test-lifecycle.mjs. That is the real drift, found by the real check, against the real previous file -- not a synthetic case.
   - A seventh script added to the alias: exit 1, naming it.
   - The desktop-target step turned into a YAML COMMENT: exit 1, naming it. A filename mentioned in a comment does not count as executed, which matters in a file that discusses these filenames at length.

3. THE DIAGNOSTICS, EXECUTED UNDER GITHUB'S OWN SHELL FLAGS -- bash --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail -- with GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY, GITHUB_WORKSPACE, RUNNER_TEMP, RUNNER_OS and RUNNER_ARCH set.
   - 'Record the machine this job ran on': exit 0, renders cores, memory, free disk, node, npm, NODE_OPTIONS and two ulimits as a table.
   - 'Why this job failed' with a V8 report present: exit 0, renders the step-outcome table and the redacted extract.
   - The same with no report anywhere: exit 0, says the job did not abort through a V8 fatal error rather than rendering nothing.
   - A DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED BY RUNNING IT UNDER THOSE FLAGS: the report search was 'find ... | head -5', which under pipefail gives find a SIGPIPE and would have aborted the diagnostics step in precisely the case it exists for. It is a read loop now. A second one: '[ cond ] && break' as the last command of a loop body exits under set -e; it is an 'if' now.

4. --report-on-fatalerror VERIFIED END TO END, not assumed. Accepted inside NODE_OPTIONS on Node 22.22.2; a forced V8 OOM produced report.<date>.<pid>.<tid>.<seq>.json; the redactor rendered event 'Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory', trigger OOMError, heap limit, committed, used, external, rss, peak rss, free and total memory, cpu seconds and the entry script's basename.

5. THE NO-SECRET-LEAKAGE CLAUSE, TESTED AS AN ATTACK RATHER THAN ASSERTED. A process was aborted with SECRET_TOKEN=hunter2-should-never-appear in its environment. grep finds the value once in the raw diagnostic report and ZERO times in the rendered summary. The raw report is never printed and never uploaded.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No GitHub runner has executed any of this. Whether 'Record the machine' and 'Why this job failed' render correctly in GitHub's own summary viewer is unverified until a run happens, and whether the exit-134 abort produces a V8 report at all is exactly the open question -- if it does not, the step says so, which is itself the next piece of evidence.

review.title: Subtitle and audio track selection, on both engines, for the first time
review.acceptance: A viewer can choose an audio track and a subtitle track, and the choice survives a candidate switch. THIS CAPABILITY DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL TODAY: there is no getTextTracks, no selectAudioLanguage, no track state and no UI anywhere in the repository, while PRODUCT_SPEC.md names 'Accessibility, subtitles, and audio correctness are core features' as a product principle and RELEASE_CRITERIA.md lists 'Audio/subtitle preferences implemented' as an MVP bar. REQUIRED: one normalised track vocabulary that both adapters answer in, so the UI never branches on engine. REQUIRED: the audio-language and subtitle-preference policy already contracted in packages/contracts/src/domains/audio.ts and subtitles.ts is the source of the DEFAULT selection, rather than a second policy being invented here. REQUIRED: forced and default subtitle flags are honoured, which the existing test matrix already lists as a playback regression scenario. REQUIRED: a selection made by the viewer is re-applied after a failover, because a candidate switch is a full teardown and losing the viewer's language on a network blip is the defect this clause exists to prevent.
review.notes:
PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. 

ROUND 107, TWO CHANGES, BOTH RECORDED AS EVENTS BEFORE THEY WERE MADE.

1. DEPENDENCY AMENDED: PW-0205 removed, PW-0202 kept. PW-0205 -> PW-0204 -> PW-0103 is blocked on the commander's Windows hardware, and it was holding the whole consumer-visible player chain (PW-0206 -> PW-0306 -> PW-0307 clause 3) behind an experiment about compositing a child HWND. This task's surface is two pure files and writes no adapter; 'a vocabulary both adapters answer in' is a contract, and a contract goes before an implementation. PW-0205 stays where it is and must answer in whatever this produces. Reverse by restoring the dependency and releasing this task.

2. CORRECTION TO A STALE PREMISE, dated round 107. The acceptance opens 'THIS CAPABILITY DOES NOT EXIST AT ALL TODAY: there is no getTextTracks, no selectAudioLanguage, no track state and no UI anywhere in the repository.' That was true when it was written and is no longer. apps/web/src/components/player/player-adapter.ts (PW-0201, DONE) declares PlayerTrack, PlayerTrackKind, getTracks(), selectAudioTrack(), selectSubtitleTrack(), a 'tracks' event and a 'trackselected' event. apps/web/src/components/player/web-player-adapter.ts (PW-0202, DONE) implements all of them against Shaka, calling getTextTracks, selectTextTrack, setTextTrackVisibility and selectAudioLanguage. packages/media-engine already holds the SELECTION POLICY -- selectAudioTrack, selectSubtitleTrack, withSelectedAudio and languageMatch with its script and macrolanguage rules -- over the contract shapes in packages/contracts/src/domains/audio.ts and subtitles.ts. EVERY 'REQUIRED' CLAUSE STANDS UNCHANGED; only the statement of what the repository contains is corrected. What is genuinely absent is this task's surface: the bridge from the engine-reported PlayerTrack list to those contract shapes, the default selection coming FROM that policy rather than from a second one invented here, forced and default flags honoured, and a viewer's explicit choice re-applied after a candidate switch. Rebuilding the vocabulary or the policy would be duplication, and the 'rather than a second policy being invented here' clause already forbids it.

3. SURFACE AMENDED, ROUND 107, recorded as task.definition_changed before any write: the adapter boundary and the Shaka adapter join the surface, four named files, because PlayerTrack is LOSSY against the policy's input in exactly the accessibility fields -- no audio `role` at all, only a boolean where subtitleKindSchema needs subtitles/sdh/forced/commentary, and no subtitle `format`. Shaka already reports all three and #readTracks drops them. Inventing them in a bridge would auto-select commentary tracks and make SDH unrepresentable, which the contracts were written to prevent. The change is additive and every new field is nullable with null meaning 'the engine did not state it'.

typecheck.evidence: npm run typecheck: 22 tasks successful, 22 total. npm run lint: 12 tasks successful, 0 errors; the single warning is a pre-existing unused import in apps/web/src/lib/db/in-memory-repository.test.ts, which is not on this surface and was not introduced here. The widened PlayerTrack compiles everywhere it is used: only two files in the repository reference the type and both are on this surface, which is why adding three required-but-nullable fields broke no caller out of reach.

unit.evidence:
npm run test: 22 tasks successful, 22 total. apps/web 85 files / 1534 tests, up from 84 / 1494 -- 40 new tests, 0 failed, nothing else disturbed. Whole repository green: provider-sdk 288, catalog-ingestion 152, backend 36, media-engine and the rest unchanged.

NEW COVERAGE, 40 CASES IN TWO FILES.
tracks.test.ts, 31 cases: codec normalisation including the RFC 6381 spellings a manifest actually states and a null for everything unrecognised; conversion with and without each assumption; the refusal to convert a sub-minimum language tag, which the contract declares .min(2) and which would otherwise build an object the schema rejects; identity and the four re-application confidences; and the resolution, including the clause this task exists for.
web-player-adapter.test.ts, 9 new cases over the three fields the adapter now reads.

THE SUITE WAS MUTATION-TESTED RATHER THAN TRUSTED, because 31 cases passing on the first run is a reason to check the tests, not to celebrate. Four mutations, each reverted:
  1. short-circuit a viewer "off" to null instead of passing the mode to the policy -> 2 failed. This is the one that matters: the contract records that a FORCED track survives an off preference, and the short circuit is the plausible implementation that deletes the only subtitle a non-reading viewer needs.
  2. let reapply match two tracks that both state no language -> 1 failed.
  3. tell the subtitle policy nothing about the audio that will actually play -> 2 failed. A forced track is keyed to the soundtrack, so this is what makes audio-before-subtitle load-bearing rather than tidy.
  4. drop the assumptions from the result -> 1 failed.
All four caught; restored, 31 passed.

THE RE-APPLICATION CLAUSE IS TESTED AS THE REAL EVENT. A candidate switch that renames EVERY id (cdn2/ prefix on all four tracks) still restores the viewer French audio and French subtitles, because a choice is remembered as a language and a purpose rather than as a track id -- WebPlayerAdapter builds audio ids as audio:<language> and takes subtitle ids from the manifest, so the ids genuinely do not survive the teardown the clause names.

ORDER-INVARIANCE IS A PROPERTY TEST, not an example: fast-check over 60 shuffles of a four-track list, asserting the same audio and subtitle answer every time. The policy claims order-invariance and this module must not reintroduce a dependency on the way in.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No browser ran any of this, no real Shaka instance produced a track list, and no mpv adapter exists to confirm it can answer in this vocabulary -- that is PW-0205 and it is sequenced after. The Shaka field names the adapter reads (audioRoles, roles, kind, mimeType, forced, channelsCount, audioCodec) are read from a fake player in the suite, as every other test in that file does; they are not verified against a running Shaka.

review.title: An LGPL-compatible libmpv and FFmpeg the product may actually ship
review.acceptance: The libmpv and FFmpeg binaries the installer ships are built under terms this product may distribute, and the evidence is recorded rather than assumed. docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 9 names two traps and RESEARCH_PLAYBACK.md already found the equivalent defect elsewhere -- 'every prebuilt ffprobe on npm is a GPL-3.0 binary, and several declare otherwise' -- so a downloaded build is not evidence of its own licence. REQUIRED: the configure flags that keep the build LGPL are stated and reproducible, and any GPL-only component is named and excluded. REQUIRED: the written-offer and attribution obligations LGPL imposes on a shipped binary are satisfied by something in the installer, not by a sentence in a README nobody ships. REQUIRED: the exact upstream versions are pinned and recorded, because PW-0207's error mapping is built against a specific header. NOT IN SCOPE: any decoder whose distribution needs a patent licence this project does not hold -- if one is required, stop and report it as a commander decision rather than shipping it.
review.notes: PROPOSED FOR gpt-architect RULING, round 80. Created unowned as part of the WINDOWS PRODUCT COMPLETION phase board so the proposal is machine-readable rather than prose, and NOT claimed before the verdict. SURFACE NOTE: this task's allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet. The evidence-based narrowing procedure applies to reconciling work already in history; for genuinely new work the surface is the smallest set of paths the acceptance can be satisfied within, and it is narrowed again from the diff before review if it turns out to be wider than what was written.

build.evidence: npm run build (turbo) at 95d8b7658065b4c52699d6e0882ed7d04a119a21: Tasks 12 successful, 12 total, exit 0. STATED PLAINLY: 11 of 12 were cache hits, because this task's surface is apps/desktop/scripts, docs/LICENSING.md and a coordination document, and none of that is a build input for any workspace. A build gate on a change the build graph cannot see is close to vacuous and saying otherwise would be a green mark that means nothing. WHAT ACTUALLY EXERCISES THIS ROUND'S CODE: node --test apps/desktop/scripts/notices.test.mjs, 17 cases, 0 failures, covering the three historical shapes of a manifest licence field, the four evidence verdicts, the filename pattern, and the rendered document's ordering, timestamp-freedom, escaping and written-offer text. collect-notices.mjs exercised end to end against a synthetic packaged tree: scoped packages, the legacy { type } manifest shape, a LICENSE-MIT file, a package with no evidence at all, and --strict exiting 1. The runtime-licence copy verified BOTH WAYS -- the generated notices carry 'No LICENSE accompanied this binary' when none is present and do not when one is. node --check on package-sidecar.mjs, collect-notices.mjs, notices.mjs and notices.test.mjs. Also clean at the same commit: npm run lint 12/12 with 0 errors (1 pre-existing warning in PW-0313's surface), npm run repo:validate, npm run ai:validate (114 tasks). THE TEST FOUND A REAL BUG IN THE FIRST ATTEMPT: the licence-filename pattern allowed only an extension, so a dual-licensed package shipping LICENSE-MIT and LICENSE-APACHE would have been reported as carrying no licence text at all. UNVERIFIED AND NOT CLAIMED: no libmpv or FFmpeg build was produced -- this container's toolchains target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -- and the notices generator has never run against a real packaged tree, because packaging happens on Windows. What the real dependency list will say is a thing the first Windows packaging run prints and nobody here can predict.
